abstract: Cigarette smoking is a well-established risk factor for the development of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet the mechanisms by which tobacco carcinogens, such as Nicotine-Derived Nitrosamine Ketone (NNK), drive pancreatic carcinogenesis remain incompletely understood. We investigated the impact of NNK on pancreatic epithelium by treating human pancreatic ductal epithelial cells (HPDE6-E6E7; H6c7) with NNK for 5 or 50 days followed by genome-wide RNA sequencing, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, comet assay, and γH2AX ELISA. We assessed γH2AX by immunohistochemistry in human PDAC tissue microarrays and in TCGA-PAAD datasets to identify clinical correlates. Acute NNK exposure (5 days) induced DNA double-strand breaks and activated ATM-γH2AX signaling, accompanied by increased RAD51 and BRCA2 recruitment, consistent with activation of homologous recombination (HR)-mediated DNA repair. In contrast, chronic NNK exposure (50 days) resulted in persistent DNA damage signaling and transcriptional upregulation of HR-associated genes, including RAD51, BRCA1, BRCA2, FANCD2, and PLK1. Despite sustained accumulation of RAD51- and BRCA2-positive repair foci, chronic NNK exposure was associated with altered RAD51 localization, persistent DNA damage, and chromosomal instability, suggesting dysregulation of HR repair fidelity during prolonged genotoxic stress. γH2AX expression was significantly elevated in NNK-treated cells, KRAS-driven premalignant pancreatic lesions, and pancreatic tissues from smokers. Increased γH2AX expression correlated with tumor progression and poor overall survival, while elevated RAD51 expression was associated with adverse outcomes in patients with PDAC. Collectively, these findings reveal a biphasic DNA damage response to NNK characterized by early activation of ATM-γH2AX-dependent DNA repair followed by persistent DNA damage signaling, dysregulated HR repair, and genomic instability during chronic exposure. Tobacco-induced disruption of DNA repair homeostasis may represent a key mechanism driving pancreatic carcinogenesis and supports γH2AX as a clinically relevant prognostic biomarker in tobacco-associated PDAC.
key_points_ko: 단기 NNK 노출(5일)은 ATM-γH2AX 신호 전달과 RAD51, BRCA2 소집을 통한 정상적인 DNA 복구 반응을 유도했습니다.
장기 NNK 노출(50일)은 지속적인 DNA 손상, RAD51 위치 이상, 염색체 불안정성 등 상동 재조합 복구 기능의 이상을 가져왔습니다.
γH2AX 및 RAD51 발현의 증가는 췌장암 환자의 암 진행 및 짧은 전체 생존기간(OS) 등 불량한 예후와 유의하게 관련되었습니다.
summary_ko: 담배 발암물질인 NNK가 췌장 상피세포에 미치는 영향을 분석한 연구입니다. 세포 연구 결과 5일간의 단기 노출 시에는 DNA 복구 기전이 활성화되었으나, 50일간의 장기 노출 시에는 지속적인 DNA 손상과 상동 재조합(HR) 복구 조절 장애, 염색체 불안정성이 유발되었습니다. 환자 데이터 분석에서 γH2AX 및 RAD51 단백질 발현 증가가 흡연자 조직 및 암 조직에서 관찰되었으며 불량한 예후와 연관되었습니다.
title: Tobacco Carcinogen Induces Persistent DNA Damage and Homologous Recombination Dysregulation in Pancreatic Ductal Carcinogenesis
title_ko: 담배 발암물질이 췌장관선암 발생 과정에서 지속적인 DNA 손상과 상동 재조합 조절 장애를 유발함을 규명한 연구
